page: Amazon Web Services i4i.large is a storage-optimized server instance featuring 2 vCPUs powered by a dedicated 3.5 GHz Intel Xeon 8375C processor with 1 physical core and 2 threads. The instance is equipped with 16.0 GB of DDR4 memory operating at 3 GHz and includes 468 GB of local NVMe SSD storage. It operates on the Nitro hypervisor and provides a baseline network bandwidth of 1 Gbps.

Benchmark data indicates average single-core performance, with a Geekbench single-core score of 1558.0 and a stress-ng single-core CPU score of 1880.58. However, due to its configuration of a single physical core, multi-core performance is limited, as reflected in a poor Geekbench multi-core score of 1806.0 and a stress-ng multi-core score of 1923.48. Memory bandwidth benchmarks also fall into the lower percentiles, with large-block read-only bandwidth at 14.18 GB/sec and write bandwidth at 13.19 GB/sec.

From a resource density perspective, the i4i.large offers a high ratio of local NVMe storage relative to its small compute footprint, making it a qualitatively cost-efficient option for workloads requiring fast local storage without needing massive CPU resources. It is suitable for small-scale database operations, low-throughput web serving, and lightweight transactional applications that benefit from low-latency NVMe storage.
